question: How can I find out who owns a given land parcel in the United States: which register holds ownership, whether it is open, and the legal route and cost to obtain it?

answer.summary: There is no national owner register found: parcel ownership is looked up county by county. In Denver and Travis County (TX), the assessor/appraisal-district search shows the tax-roll owner by address, parcel or account number, while the county recorder/clerk holds the recorded deeds. Both web searches are open; published fees are for copies (Travis: name search free, $1/page, $5 certification; Denver: certified $1 + $0.25/page). The tax-roll owner is not the deed. Bulk owner files exist (TCAD free export; Regrid paid); federal original patents are at BLM GLO.
main_caveats: Only Denver (CO) and Travis County (TX) were tested; other states use towns, parishes or registries of deeds and may differ. They were not checked.
The tax-roll owner is not the title: TCAD says its data is 'purely for ad valorem taxation purposes' and it corrects owners from deeds recorded with the County Clerk.
No recorded-document search was executed: Travis's search returned a Cloudflare challenge (403) to curl and Denver's guest entry could not be completed by script.
Owners can be withheld: TCAD's export layout has confidential-owner flags and Travis says records restricted by law or court order are not online.
Search keys differ: Denver's recorder search is by owner name (last, first); the assessor is by address, Parcel ID or schedule number. Look up the parcel first.
This card explains lookup of a specified parcel; do not build owner inventories from bulk exports (TCAD, Regrid).

steps: Identify the county and the parcel's owner on the assessor/appraisal roll.
Search the county recorder/clerk portal by name (Denver: last, first) and open the deed by reception/instrument number.
For official proof request a certified copy: Denver via the portal prompt ($1 per document + $0.25 per page); Travis by phone/email/in person ($5 per document + $1 per page).
For pre-electronic periods ask the office: Travis charges $10 per name per ten-year period for microfilm/paper searches.
reading_traps: A name search returns all instruments for that name, not parcels; confirm the legal description.
Free online copies are watermarked 'unofficial copy' (Travis).
The recording fee ($25 first page in Travis) is the cost to file, not to search.
